name: Bhringraj / False daisy / Eclipta Alba

sections.description_of_plant:
Bhringraj (Eclipta alba / Eclipta prostrata) is a low-growing, creeping herb that typically reaches a height of about 30–60 cm. It is an annual, erect or spreading plant, often branching from the base and capable of rooting at nodes where it touches the ground. The stems are green or purplish, cylindrical, and slightly hairy. The plant bears small, white, daisy-like flowers (around 6–8 mm in diameter), typically found on short stalks (peduncles) arising from the axils of leaves or at branch tips. The leaves are opposite, oblong-lanceolate, and have a slightly rough texture. 
 General Information 
 Bhringraj (Eclipta alba) is commonly called false daisy. The Sanskrit names of Bhringraj are “Bhringraj” and “Tekarajah” and common Hindi names are “Bhangra” and “Bhangro”. It is one main herb that is used in hair dyes. China and Brazil are using this herb as anti-venom for snake poisoning. It is a common weed in India throughout waste grounds. 
 In Ayurveda Bhringraj (Eclipta alba) is considered to be “rasayana”, herb for longevity and rejuvenation. Main principle of Ayurveda is to balance tridosha. This herb works wonderfully on tridosha and maintains their imbalance. Bhringraj is a wonderful herb used in AYURVEDA for hair care and cirrhosis. It rejuvenates memory, hair, teeth, bones, vision and hearing. This herb is rich in several bioactive compounds, notably ecliptine, along with wedelolactone, demethyl wedelolactone, flavonoids, and alkaloids, which contribute to its therapeutic benefits. Leaves of this plant are rich in proteins and extract is resinous in nature. It is a general tonic in case of debility. The herb is antioxidant, analgesic, antiviral, antibacterial, anticancer and hepato-protective in nature. It also contains wedelolactone, amyrin, heptacosanol, hentriacontane and stigmasterol.
